name: cloneworx Backup
author: icecoke

sections.description:
Easy backup. Safe restore.

cloneworx Backup backs up the database and the files of your WordPress website to storage that belongs to you: a local folder, FTP/FTPS, SFTP, WebDAV, Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage, Google Drive or Dropbox. Backups travel directly from your server to your storage. You need no account at cloneworx, and no backup ever passes through a server of cloneworx.

A backup is worth what its restore is worth. Every restore starts with a pre-check, and the previous state of your website is kept for seven days, so a restore can be undone with one click.

Guides for every page of the plugin: help.cloneworx.de

Where your backups go

  • Local folder on your server, chosen with a folder browser.
  • FTP and FTPS
  • SFTP with a password or a private key; the key of the server is checked.
  • WebDAV
  • Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage with your own access key.
  • Google Drive: you sign in with Google, and the plugin sees only the files it created itself.
  • Dropbox: you sign in with Dropbox, and the plugin sees only its own app folder.

You can set up several targets, also several of the same type.

Why cloneworx Backup

  • A restore with a way back. Before anything is written, a pre-check compares the backup with your website and shows every difference in plain words. After the restore you have seven days to keep it or to undo it.
  • Made for ordinary hosting. A backup never runs in one piece. It works in short steps and saves its state several times per second. When the server stops a step, the next one continues from the last saved point.
  • You hear about it when backups stop. An email on errors and warnings, and a warning when the last good backup is older than the plan allows. WordPress Site Health shows the same state.
  • Verified when written. Every part of a backup is verified when it is written. “Check backup” reads a stored backup the way a restore would, without writing anything.
  • Backups that are not tied to one server. Files are stored by named roots with relative paths, never with absolute server paths, so that a backup can be restored cleanly on another server or path.
  • Backups you find again. Every target keeps an index and a catalog, so that backups can be found and imported again from any target or file with a single click.
  • Only what you need on screen. A compact view for every day and an extended view with every detail.
  • Protected credentials. The passwords and keys of your targets are stored encrypted with a key of the plugin’s own, protected by the security keys in your wp-config.php.
  • In your language. English, German, Spanish, French and Dutch.

Features

  • Backup plans with a schedule: every 1, 2, 4, 6 or 12 hours, daily, weekly or monthly, in the time zone of your website.
  • You choose per plan what is backed up: database, plugins, themes, uploads, must-use plugins, the rest of wp-content, the WordPress core and the files of the root folder.
  • Exclusion rules for files and folders.
  • The database is backed up completely. For single tables that only grow and are not needed to run the site (sessions, logs, caches, statistics), you can switch off the rows table by table: such a table is recreated empty on restore.
  • Database snapshot, a switch per plan that is on by default: all tables are read as of the same moment, even when the export takes several steps (InnoDB).
  • Retention per plan and target: you set how many backups stay, older ones are removed. The newest good backup is never removed.
  • Lock a backup, for example before a big update: it is never deleted automatically.
  • Restore the database, the files or both.
  • Download a backup from a local folder as a single file and import it again, on this website or on another one. The upload runs in chunks, so that large files work behind upload limits.
  • A scheduler that detects missed runs and names the next step.
  • A support report that you copy or download yourself. Nothing is sent automatically.
  • Every function on the command line with WP-CLI (wp cloneworx-backup).
  • A Quick Start on the Overview leads from the first target to the first backup.

Your First Backup

  1. Install and activate cloneworx Backup under Plugins > Add New, or upload the zip file there.
  2. Open the plugin in the menu “cloneworx” and go to the Targets page. Click “Add target”, choose where your backups go and save. Saving runs a connection test.
  3. Click “Back up now” on the Overview. This is your first backup 😉
  4. With your first target the plugin has created the plan “Daily backup”. It is paused until you switch it on, on the Backups page.

External services

The plugin sends data only to the storage targets you set up yourself, and only for the purpose of storing and restoring your backups. For every target: the plugin sends the login data of that target, the backups of this website (database and files) with their info file, index and catalog, and, as with every server request, the IP address of your web server. This happens with every backup to that target and when you test the connection, check, delete, clean up, search or restore backups there. Never to anyone else. The support report and the plugin’s log files stay on your site; you copy or download them yourself.

  • FTP/FTPS, SFTP, WebDAV: the server from the settings of the target; you choose it and you are responsible for it. FTP with the encryption “None” and WebDAV over http:// travel in clear text. FTPS is encrypted, but the plugin does not check the certificate of the FTP server (the FTP extension of PHP cannot). SFTP is always encrypted and checks the key of the server; with a private key only a proof is sent, the key itself never leaves the web server. The plugin never follows a redirect to another address.
  • Amazon S3 and S3-compatible storage: the bucket at its Amazon S3 address (https://BUCKET.s3.REGION.amazonaws.com, with the name of your bucket and its region) or at the address from the settings of the target, with no service of cloneworx in between. Sent are the access key and, with every request, a signature made with the secret key (the secret key never leaves the web server). If no region is entered, the connection test first asks Amazon S3 for the region of the bucket. Amazon S3 is a service of Amazon Web Services: terms https://aws.amazon.com/service-terms/, privacy https://aws.amazon.com/privacy/. For an S3-compatible service the terms and the privacy policy of your provider apply.
  • Google Drive: the Google Drive API (https://www.googleapis.com), with an access token on every request; the plugin asks only for the permission to see and manage the files it created itself (scope drive.file). Google Drive is a service of Google: terms https://policies.google.com/terms, privacy https://policies.google.com/privacy.
  • Dropbox: the Dropbox API (https://api.dropboxapi.com and https://content.dropboxapi.com), with an access token on every request; the plugin sees only the folder that Dropbox keeps for the app (access type “App folder”) and asks for the permissions account_info.read, files.metadata.read, files.content.read and files.content.write. When you remove the target, connect it again or delete the plugin with the switch that removes all settings, the plugin asks Dropbox to revoke the access; if that request fails, the access stays valid until you disconnect the app in your Dropbox account. Dropbox is a service of Dropbox, Inc.: terms https://www.dropbox.com/terms, privacy https://www.dropbox.com/privacy.

auth.cloneworx.de: sign-in relay for Google Drive and Dropbox

What it is: https://auth.cloneworx.de is a service of cloneworx (viavell GmbH & Co. KG, Bremen, Germany). The plugin uses it for one purpose only: to connect a Google Drive or Dropbox target. Both providers require a client secret that cannot be shipped inside a plugin, so this service holds the secret, passes the sign-in on to Google or Dropbox and stores nothing.

What is sent and when: only after you click “Connect with Google” or “Connect with Dropbox”, never before and never without a Google Drive or Dropbox target. Your browser sends the address of the admin page of this website, a random value and the language. Your web server sends the code of the sign-in and, whenever a new access token is needed (about once an hour for Google, every few hours for Dropbox, while the target is in use), the stored refresh token. As with every request, the IP addresses of browser and web server are transmitted. Never a backup, a file or the address of your Google or Dropbox account.

Terms of service: https://help.cloneworx.de/hc/de/articles/30703520611612 (German)
Privacy policy: https://help.cloneworx.de/hc/de/articles/30704317462940 (German)

Third-party licenses

The admin interface of this plugin is a bundled JavaScript application. It contains third-party components under the MIT, BSD 3-Clause, 0BSD and Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licenses, all of them GPL-compatible according to the license list of the Free Software Foundation (https://www.gnu.org/licenses/license-list.html). The components, their copyright holders, versions and license texts are shipped in the folder licenses/ of this plugin (one file per component, index in licenses/components.json) and are listed on the plugin’s Settings page under “Licenses”. The SFTP target uses the PHP library phpseclib (MIT) with its dependencies paragonie/constant_time_encoding and paragonie/random_compat (MIT), shipped unchanged in the folder vendor/ of this plugin and listed in the same places. Icons are from Font Awesome Free by Fonticons, Inc. (https://fontawesome.com); only the SVG icon packages are bundled, no fonts. Brand icons are trademarks of their respective owners and are used only to represent the respective service.

Trademarks

cloneworx is a trademark of viavell GmbH & Co. KG. All other names and logos of third parties are the property of their respective owners. This does not imply any affiliation or partnership.
sections.faq:
Is there a comprehensive knowledge base and help center?

Yes! At https://help.cloneworx.de, you’ll find comprehensive, constantly updated documentation, FAQs, a community, and the option to get direct support from the developers.

What does the plugin need?

WordPress 6.2 or later and PHP 7.4 or later, with a MySQL or MariaDB database. On a 32-bit PHP the plugin works with a size limit of 1.5 GiB per backup: it warns in the dashboard, and a backup or restore that would exceed the limit stops and says so, because larger sizes cannot be counted safely there. WordPress Multisite is not supported. Target types that your server cannot use are greyed out with the reason.

Can I undo a restore?

Yes. The previous state of your website is kept for seven days. During that time the Restore page offers “Keep restore” and “Undo restore”.

Does the plugin send my data to anyone?

Only to the storage targets you set up yourself. To connect Google Drive or Dropbox, the sign-in runs through auth.cloneworx.de. What is sent, when and to whom is listed under “External services” in the description.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: the plan editor is arranged in groups. A 3-2-1 status shows the number of copies, the kinds of storage and the copies in another building; each target has a field “Location” for it.
  • New: a backup that this website does not know (found again at a target, imported, or written by an earlier version) is restored only after you have confirmed it as correct. The plugin notices when a backup was changed at its target.
  • New: global log in the settings.
  • New: the tile “Backups” on the Restore page works like the one on the Backups page. “Restore” in the menu of a backup opens the preparation for exactly this backup.
  • New: the progress line names the target a backup is being sent to.
  • New: when a running operation blocks another action, the plugin says so.
  • New: connections for the separate plugin cloneworx Backup Pro (several targets per plan, plans every 5 to 30 minutes, retention by age, encrypted backups, exclusions per plan, deleting several backups at once).
  • Changed: one backup plan can be active at a time. “Back up now” works for every plan.
  • Changed: exclusion rules understand ** for any number of folders, as in .gitignore. The default exclusions include .git.
  • Changed: buttons follow one rule. Actions that change or remove something (delete, restore) are red.
  • Changed: deleting an entry that has no backup at any target says so.
  • Fixed: the list of backups did not refresh when a run started and ended between two refreshes of the page.
  • Fixed: corrections in the German, Spanish, French and Dutch texts.

1.0.0

  • First public release.
